Hon'ble Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I,J.
1.
Heard Sri Mukesh Kumar Tewari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Anurag Verma, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant for quashing the impugned order dated 29.04.2023 passed by learned Additional Session Judge-II, Court No.2,
Lakhimpur Kheri in S. T. No.395 of 2015 "State vs. Vakeel and others", under Sections 363, 366,
376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3 (2) (v) of SC/ST Act in Case Crime No.55 of 2013, Police Station Ishanagar, District Lakhimpur Kheri.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that a first information report came to be lodged under Sections 363, 366 I.P.C. against the accused person, namely, Shrawan Pasi.
The present applicant was not named in the first information report.
His name is not mentioned in the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
However, as a belated attempt to falsely implicate the present applicant, the victim named the present applicant.

His further submission is that the present applicant has been summoned in exercise of power vested with the learned trial Court under Section 319 Cr.P.C.

The learned trial Court, while passing the order dated 16.03.2022, under Section 319 Cr.P.C., has placed reliance on the statements of P.W.-1, complainant, Bansi Lal and P.W.-2, victim and based on aforesaid statements and placing reliance thereon, the applicant has been summoned to stand trial under Sections 363, 366, 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3 (2) 5 SC/ST Act.
4.

It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the aforesaid order dated 16.03.2022 has been passed without recording the satisfaction as required to be recorded by the learned trial Court having regard to law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Hardeep Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2014) 3 SCC 92.
5.

entities.text: Hardeep Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2014) 3 SCC 92
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that during the pendency of present proceeding,
the process has come to be issued against the present applicant which is nothing but an abuse of process of this Court.
On the basis of aforesaid submissions, he has submitted that the impugned order deserves to be quashed.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer by submitting that though the present applicant was neither named in the first information report nor there was any averment against him in the statement of victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
However, the first informant and the victim have been examined as P.W.-1 and P.W.-2 in the learned trial Court.

On the basis of their statements which are cogent and reliable and worthy of clinching conviction,
the learned trial Court has proceeded to pass the impugned order dated 29.04.2023 which cannot be faulted on the ground which is being argued by learned counsel for the applicant.
7. Thus, in view of aforesaid, learned A.G.A. has submitted that the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is devoid of merit and deserves to be dismissed.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and upon perusal of record, this Court finds that initially a first information report came to be lodged under Sections 363 and 366 I.P.C. against the accused person, namely, Shrawan Pasi only.
However, upon conclusion of investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against him and two other accused persons.

It also transpires that during the course of trial of S. T. No.395 of 2015 "State vs. Vakeel and others", an application bearing no.18Kha under Sections 319 Cr.P.C. came to be moved from the side of prosecution for summoning the Munna Lal and Kennu as accused.

The learned trial Court vide order dated 16.03.2022, proceeded to summon the present applicant, namely, Munna Lal and one accused, namely, Kennu under Sections 363, 366, 376, 506 I.P.C. and 3 (2) 5 SC/ST Act which was based on the statements of first informant and the victim, who have been examined as P.W.-1 and P.W.-2 in the learned trial Court.

9. Having scrutinized the evidence available on record, at this stage, this Court is of the considered view that no ground exists for quashing the impugned order dated 29.04.2023 as the same does not appear to be illegal or perverse.
The same is not an instance of abuse of process of this Court also.
